title: 4. Effects of salt as a corn-supplement intake limiter and forage maturity on intake, digestibility, and ruminal fermentation in beef cattle grazing wheat pasture.
content:
Abstract
Salt (NaCl) is commonly included in beef cattle supplements to limit intake. However, its effects on forage intake and ruminal fermentation in beef cattle grazing wheat pasture are not well defined. Therefore, the objective of this study was to evaluate the effects of NaCl inclusion in a corn supplement and forage stage of maturity on forage intake and ruminal fermentation characteristics of cannulated cows grazing wheat pasture. Angus-crossbred ruminally cannulated cows [n = 8; bodyweight (BW) = 806 ± 82.5 kg] grazing wheat pasture were utilized in a crossover design with two 14-d periods (10 d adaptation; 4 d collection). Treatments were ground corn at 0.4% BW/d (CON) or ground corn at 0.4% BW/d plus NaCl at 0.1% BW/d (SALT). Wheat pasture maturity stages were March (MAR; early vegetative) and April (APR; early reproductive). Cows grazed a single wheat pasture and were supplemented via the rumen cannula twice daily at 0700 and 1900 h. Chromic oxide (16 g/d) was dosed intraruminally from d 6 to 14, and fecal samples were collected throughout the 4-d collection period and composited by period to estimate intake. Rumen fluid was analyzed for pH, ammonia-N, and volatile fatty acid (VFA) concentrations. Data were analyzed using PROC GLM (intake and digestibility) and PROC MIXED (ruminal fermentation) with fixed effects of treatment, maturity stage, and their interaction. Significance was declared at P ≤ 0.10. Forage intake and total DMI were not affected by SALT (P ≥ 0.14). Crude protein (CP) intake was lower for SALT than CON (1.35 vs 2.01 ± 0.15 kg/d; P = 0.009), and lower for MAR than APR (1.46 vs 1.90 ± 0.15 kg/d; P = 0.055). Intake of NDF was higher for MAR than APR (P = 0.09). A treatment × maturity interaction was detected for CP digestibility (P ≤ 0.03). Digestibility of CP was not affected in MAR by SALT (P = 0.63) but APR was lower for SALT (P = 0.005). Digestibility of NDF and OM was greater in MAR than in APR (P ≤ 0.001). Ruminal concentration of ammonia-N (5.94 vs 3.50 ± 0.31 mM; P ≤ 0.001), total VFA (134.82 vs 105.17 ± 4.31 mM; P ≤ 0.001), and butyrate (15.92 vs 12.92 ± 0.54 mol/100 mol; P = 0.002) decreased for SALT. Acetate increased (51.41 vs 54.59 ± 1.03 mol/100 mol; P = 0.05), and ruminal pH was not affected (P = 0.12) by SALT. As wheat pasture matured, ammonia-N (2.52 vs 6.93 ± 0.31 mM; P < 0.0001) and total VFA concentration (111.53 vs 128.46 ± 4.31 mM; for MAR and APR, respectively) increased (P ≤ 0.016). Overall, NaCl inclusion in a corn-based supplement altered ruminal fermentation without affecting wheat forage intake.
